1	# Repair an inconsistent alloy equilibrium assessment
2	
3	A materials-thermodynamics group is replaying literature-linked alloy studies
4	with the supplied historical pycalphad source and databases. The calculations
5	complete and return finite datasets, but several observations no longer agree
6	with the group's archived results:
7	
8	- a composition-temperature phase boundary moves when an equivalent database
9	  representation is admitted to the same assessment;
10	- the associated phase fractions and internal-state evolution cease to form a
11	  physically consistent transition;
12	- chemical-potential and heat-response curves disagree with the corresponding
13	  baseline calculation; and
14	- the equilibrium topology depends on a representation that should not create
15	  a new thermodynamic state for the requested components.
16	
17	Run the offline workflow, inspect the databases and source snapshot, and repair
18	the scientific
19	implementation. Determine the common cause rather than treating the symptoms
20	independently. The repair must generalize to other valid CALPHAD database
21	representations and supported phase states while preserving public APIs and
22	unrelated model behavior.
23	
24	Do not hard-code the supplied grids or generated artifacts, and do not modify
25	the scientific input files. The public workflow only establishes that the real
26	project calculation runs and saves results; correctness is evaluated on
27	independent scientific cases.

1	# Full assessment case study: one lattice represented by ordered positions
2	
3	## Scope and source
4	
5	This note explains a general compound-energy-formalism representation used by
6	the complete Al-Ni assessment distributed with the historical project:
7	
8	`source/examples/NI_AL_DUPIN_2001.TDB`
9	
10	It is a complete assessment with liquid, compound, BCC, and FCC phase
11	families, magnetic terms, interaction parameters, and literature references.
12	The public `study_beta` calculation requests `LIQUID`, `AL3NI1`, `AL3NI2`,
13	`AL3NI5`, `BCC_A2`, `BCC_B2`, `FCC_A1`, and `FCC_L12` through the normal
14	database and equilibrium workflow. The declarations and parameter blocks in
15	the TDB remain the authoritative scientific input; this note explains how to
16	read one representation pattern within that larger assessment.
17	
18	## The FCC phase family in the assessment
19	
20	The assessment contains both a disordered FCC description and an ordered
21	L1_2 description. Their constituent layouts are:
22	
23	| Description | Substitutional position classes | Site ratios | Additional sublattice |
24	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
25	| Disordered FCC_A1 | one class occupied by AL or NI | `1` | a VA-only sublattice with ratio `1` |
26	| Ordered FCC_L12 | two classes, each occupied by AL or NI | `0.75`, `0.25` | the same VA-only sublattice with ratio `1` |
27	
28	In TDB notation, the corresponding declarations are:
29	
30	```text
31	PHASE FCC_A1  %)  2 1   1 !
32	CONSTITUENT FCC_A1  :AL,NI : VA : !
33	
34	PHASE FCC_L12  %*+  3 .75   .25   1 !
35	CONSTITUENT FCC_L12  :AL,NI : AL,NI : VA : !
36	```
37	
38	The complete endmember, interaction, magnetic, and ordering parameter blocks
39	immediately following these declarations must be interpreted together. The
40	two declaration snippets are therefore not a standalone model and are not a
41	separate input to run.
42	
43	## Physical interpretation
44	
45	The `0.75` and `0.25` classes are two symmetry-distinct position classes of
46	the same physical FCC substitutional lattice. They do not add another mole of
47	material. They partition the parent substitutional lattice so that different
48	AL/NI occupancies can describe long-range atomic order.
49	
50	In compound-energy-formalism language, multiple ordered positions can
51	therefore represent one physical parent sublattice. The position variables
52	describe how that parent occupancy is distributed among symmetry-distinct
53	classes.
54	
55	Bulk occupancy is obtained by weighting the occupancies of the ordered
56	position classes by their site ratios. Consequently:
57	
58	- if the AL/NI fractions are the same on both ordered position classes, the
59	  position split carries no long-range ordering information and represents a
60	  disordered occupancy of the same physical substitutional lattice;
61	- if the fractions differ, the extra internal degrees of freedom describe an
62	  ordered state while preserving the aggregate composition; and
63	- the VA-only sublattice remains a separate part of the phase model rather than
64	  being created by the ordering split.
65	
66	This is a coordinate relationship between scientific representations, not a
67	claim that every multisublattice phase is equivalent to a single-sublattice
68	phase. A valid relationship also depends on the declared site ratios,
69	constituent sets, linked phase descriptions, active components, and the full
70	thermodynamic contributions in the assessment.
71	
72	## Consequences for complete calculations
73	
74	A complete order-disorder assessment can combine several effects at once:
75	
76	- a baseline contribution associated with the disordered phase family;
77	- additional energetic terms that distinguish ordered occupancies;
78	- ideal and excess configurational contributions;
79	- magnetic contributions; and
80	- vacancy or interstitial position classes that are not part of the ordering
81	  partition.
82	
83	Equivalent database descriptions may use a different number of internal
84	position variables while describing the same physical lattice and aggregate
85	composition. When the descriptions and all their contributions correspond,
86	the choice of internal coordinates should not by itself create a new physical
87	equilibrium state. Conversely, a similar-looking constituent array is not
88	enough to establish equivalence without the complete assessment semantics.
89	
90	## Where to continue reading
91	
92	- `source/examples/NI_AL_DUPIN_2001.TDB` contains the complete phase and
93	  parameter definitions summarized above.
94	- `source/docs/examples/EquilibriumWithOrdering.rst` follows ordering behavior
95	  through full equilibrium calculations for Al-Fe and Al-Ni.
96	- `source/docs/examples/UsingCalculationResults.rst` defines phase fractions,
97	  site fractions, internal degrees of freedom, and result dimensions.
98	- `paper_assets/pycalphad_jors_2017.md` gives the project-level CALPHAD,
99	  compound-energy-formalism, equilibrium, and software context.

The emphasis on "representation that should not create a new thermodynamic state for the requested components" — maybe the bug relates to composition accounting (`mole_fraction_from_site_fraction`?) or to the `MODEL` definition causing different Gibbs energies. 

Actually, there is a classic pycalphad-era bug in `pycalphad/model.py` around `equilibrium` in `pycalphad/core/equilibrium.py`: `_adjust_conditions`/`_compute_equilibrium`... Hmm.

Let me think about the "common cause": An equivalent representation is "admitted to the same assessment" — e.g., in the benchmark TDB there is `BCC_A2` and `BCC_4SL` (4-sublattice representation of BCC, site ratios 0.5/0.5 maybe) plus `BCC_R1`/`BCC_R2` (other representations). When the ordered 4-sublattice representation is included along with BCC_A2 disordered, results change because pycalphad computes mole fractions from site fractions incorrectly — weighting by site ratio. Specifically, in `pycalphad/core/eqsolver.pyx` or in `pycalphad/model.py` there's a function converting site fractions to mole fractions: the sum over sublattices of site_ratio * site_fraction. If the bug multiplies wrongly (e.g., uses per-sublattice totals but then divides by a wrong normalizer), then the composition constraint in the equilibrium solve would be wrong for multi-sublattice phases.

Now I understand the database. The benchmark TDB includes `DIS_PART` type definitions (`AMEND_PHASE_DESCRIPTION BCC_4SL DIS_PART BCC_A2` etc.) — the partitioned-model order/disorder treatment. pycalphad 0.8.4 has support for this in `tdb.py` via `model_hints` — when a phase has `DIS_PART`, the Model's ordered phase gets a "disordered phase" hint and pycalphad builds a model combining: G_total = G_disordered + G_ordering (where the ordering part is computed from the ordered endmembers minus disordered contribution). Actually Thermo-Calc's DIS_PART mechanics: the ordered phase uses the same constitution space; the disordered phase's parameters contribute to it. In pycalphad, this is implemented in `Model.__init__` via `model_hints['ordered_phase']` etc.? Hmm, no.

Actually wait — DIS_PART in pycalphad: In `tdb.py`, `_process_type_definition` handles 'DIS_ORDERED' / 'DIS_PART' keywords, and records `dbf._structure_dict[phase_name] = {'disordered_phase': ..., 'ordered_phase': ...}`? Then in `pycalphad/model.py`, `Model.build_phase(dbf, phase_name, dbf.symbols, model_hints=dbf._models)` where if model_hints has 'disordered_phase', it merges parameters? Hmm, I recall pycalphad handles this by adding the disordered phase's parameters into the ordered phase's model with mole fractions mapped... Let me actually read the code.

But hold on — Thermo-Calc order/disorder option: with DIS_PART, the *ordered* phase contains the sum: G_ord = G_dis + G_ord(the extra params). 490	        """
491	        Replace y_i -> y_i + (1 - sum(y involved in parameter)) / m,
492	        where m is the arity of the interaction parameter.
493	        Returns a dict converting the list of Symbols (comps) to this.
494	        m is assumed equal to the length of comps.
495	
496	        When incorporating binary, ternary or n-ary interaction parameters
497	        into systems with more than n components, the sum of site fractions
498	        involved in the interaction parameter may no longer be unity. This
499	        breaks the symmetry of the parameter. The solution suggested by
500	        Muggianu, 1975, is to renormalize the site fractions by replacing them
501	        with a term that will sum to unity even in higher-order systems.
502	        There are other solutions that involve retaining the asymmetry for
503	        physical reasons, but this solution works well for components that
504	        are physically similar.
505	
506	        This procedure is based on an analysis by Hillert, 1980,
507	        published in the Calphad journal.
508	        """
509	        arity = len(comps)
510	        return_dict = {}
511	        correction_term = (S.One - Add(*comps)) / arity
512	        for comp in comps:
513	            return_dict[comp] = comp + correction_term
514	        return return_dict

import numpy as np
from pycalphad import Database, Model, variables as v

def disordered_limit_check(dbf_path, comps, ord_phase, dis_phase, occupancy):
    """occupancy: dict species->fraction for substitutional sublattices."""
    dbf = Database(dbf_path)
    mod_dis = Model(dbf, comps, dis_phase)
    mod_ord = Model(dbf, comps, ord_phase)
    T = 1200.0
    # state for disordered model
    state_dis = {v.T: T, v.P: 101325.}
    for k in mod_dis.variables:
        if isinstance(k, v.SiteFraction):
            state_dis[k] = occupancy.get(k.species.name, 1.0 if k.species.name == 'VA' else 0.0)
    state_ord = {v.T: T, v.P: 101325.}
    for k in mod_ord.variables:
        if isinstance(k, v.SiteFraction):
            state_ord[k] = occupancy.get(k.species.name, 1.0 if k.species.name == 'VA' else 0.0)
    # disordered state of ordered phase: same occupancy in every non-VA sublattice
    ed = float(mod_dis.energy.xreplace(state_dis))
    eo = float(mod_ord.energy.xreplace(state_ord))
    eord = float(mod_ord.models['ord'].xreplace(state_ord))
    print(f'{ord_phase}/{dis_phase}: G_dis={ed:.6f} G_ord={eo:.6f} ord_contrib={eord:.6f} diff={eo-ed:.6e}')

172	    def obj_hessian(self, x_in):
173	        cdef CompositionSet compset = self.composition_sets[0]
174	        cdef size_t num_statevars = len(compset.phase_record.state_variables)
175	        cdef double[:, ::1] hess = np.zeros((self.num_vars, self.num_vars))
176	        cdef double[::1] hess_tmp = np.zeros((self.num_vars * self.num_vars))
177	        cdef double[::1] grad_tmp = np.zeros(self.num_vars)
178	        cdef double[:, ::1] hess_tmp_view
179	        cdef double[::1] x = np.array(x_in)
180	        cdef double[::1] x_tmp = np.zeros(x.shape[0])
181	        cdef double phase_frac = 0
182	        cdef size_t var_idx = 0
183	        cdef size_t phase_idx, grad_idx, cons_idx, dof_idx, sv_idx
184	        cdef size_t row, col
185	        cdef size_t constraint_offset = 0
186	        x_tmp[:num_statevars] = x[:num_statevars]
187	        var_idx = num_statevars
188	        for phase_idx in range(self.num_phases):
189	            compset = self.composition_sets[phase_idx]
190	            phase_frac = x[self.num_vars - self.num_phases + phase_idx]
191	            x_tmp[num_statevars:num_statevars+compset.phase_record.phase_dof] = \
192	                x[var_idx:var_idx+compset.phase_record.phase_dof]
193	            hess_tmp_view = <double[:num_statevars+compset.phase_record.phase_dof,
194	                                    :num_statevars+compset.phase_record.phase_dof]>&hess_tmp[0]
195	            compset.phase_record.grad(grad_tmp, x_tmp)
196	            compset.phase_record.hess(hess_tmp_view, x_tmp)
197	            for row in range(compset.phase_record.phase_dof):
198	                for col in range(compset.phase_record.phase_dof):
199	                    hess[var_idx+row, var_idx+col] = \
200	                        phase_frac * hess_tmp_view[num_statevars+row, num_statevars+col]
201	                    hess[var_idx+col, var_idx+row] = \

203	            for iter_idx in range(num_statevars):
204	                for dof_idx in range(compset.phase_record.phase_dof):
205	                    hess[iter_idx, var_idx + dof_idx] += \
206	                        phase_frac * hess_tmp_view[iter_idx, num_statevars + dof_idx]

209	                for sv_idx in range(num_statevars):
210	                    hess[iter_idx, sv_idx] += \
211	                        phase_frac * hess_tmp_view[iter_idx, sv_idx]
212	                    if iter_idx != sv_idx:
213	                        hess[sv_idx, iter_idx] += \
214	                            phase_frac * hess_tmp_view[iter_idx, sv_idx]
215	            # wrt phase_frac
216	            for dof_idx in range(compset.phase_record.phase_dof):
217	                hess[self.num_vars - self.num_phases + phase_idx, var_idx + dof_idx] = grad_tmp[num_statevars+dof_idx]
218	                hess[var_idx + dof_idx, self.num_vars - self.num_phases + phase_idx] = grad_tmp[num_statevars+dof_idx]
219	            for sv_idx in range(num_statevars):
220	                hess[self.num_vars - self.num_phases + phase_idx, sv_idx] = grad_tmp[sv_idx]
221	                hess[sv_idx, self.num_vars - self.num_phases + phase_idx] = grad_tmp[sv_idx]
222	            hess_tmp[:] = 0
223	            grad_tmp[:] = 0

239	        cdef int idx, phase_idx, idx_row, idx_col, iter_idx, cons_idx

242	        # First: Fixed degree of freedom constraints (linear)
243	        constraint_offset += self.num_fixed_dof_constraints
244	
245	        # Second: Phase internal constraints
246	        var_idx = num_statevars

259	                                                  constraint_hess_tmp_view[cons_idx, idx_row, idx_col]
260	                        if idx_row != idx_col:
261	                            hess[idx_col, idx_row] += lmul[constraint_offset + cons_idx] * \
262	                                                    constraint_hess_tmp_view[cons_idx, idx_col, idx_row]
263	                for idx_row in range(compset.phase_record.phase_dof):
264	                    for idx_col in range(idx_row, compset.phase_record.phase_dof):
265	                        hess[var_idx + idx_row, var_idx + idx_col] += lmul[constraint_offset + cons_idx] * \
266	                                                  constraint_hess_tmp_view[cons_idx, num_statevars+idx_row, num_statevars+idx_col]

269	                                                  constraint_hess_tmp_view[cons_idx, num_statevars+idx_col, num_statevars+idx_row]

271	            constraint_hess_tmp[:] = 0
272	            x_tmp[num_statevars:] = 0

276	        var_idx = num_statevars
277	        # Third: Multiphase constraints
278	        for phase_idx in range(self.num_phases):
279	            compset = self.composition_sets[phase_idx]
280	            spidx = self.num_vars - self.num_phases + phase_idx
281	            x_tmp[num_statevars:num_statevars+compset.phase_record.phase_dof] = \

292	                                                  constraint_hess_tmp_view[cons_idx, idx_row, idx_col]

299	                                                  constraint_hess_tmp_view[cons_idx, num_statevars+idx_row, num_statevars+idx_col]

301	                            hess[var_idx + idx_col, var_idx + idx_row] += lmul[constraint_offset + cons_idx] * \

347	    def mass_jacobian(self, x_in):
348	        """For chemical potential calculation."""
349	        cdef CompositionSet compset = self.composition_sets[0]
350	        cdef int num_statevars = len(compset.phase_record.state_variables)
351	        cdef np.ndarray active_ineq = np.flatnonzero((np.array(x_in) <= 1.1*MIN_SITE_FRACTION))
352	        cdef size_t num_active_ineq = len(active_ineq)
353	        cdef double[:, ::1] mass_jac = np.zeros((self.num_internal_constraints + num_active_ineq + len(self.nonvacant_elements), self.num_vars))
354	        cdef double[:, ::1] mass_jac_tmp = np.zeros((self.num_internal_constraints + len(self.nonvacant_elements), self.num_vars))
355	        cdef double[:, ::1] mass_jac_tmp_view, mass_grad
356	        cdef double[::1] x = np.array(x_in)
357	        cdef double[::1] x_tmp
358	        cdef int var_idx = 0
359	        cdef int phase_idx, grad_idx
360	        cdef int constraint_offset = 0
361	        # First: Phase internal constraints
362	        var_idx = num_statevars
363	        for phase_idx in range(self.num_phases):
364	            compset = self.composition_sets[phase_idx]
365	            x_tmp = np.r_[x[:num_statevars], x[var_idx:var_idx+compset.phase_record.phase_dof]]
366	            mass_jac_tmp_view = <double[:compset.phase_record.num_internal_cons,
367	                                              :num_statevars+compset.phase_record.phase_dof]>&mass_jac_tmp[0,0]
368	            compset.phase_record.internal_cons_jac(mass_jac_tmp_view, x_tmp)
369	            mass_jac[constraint_offset:constraint_offset + compset.phase_record.num_internal_cons,
370	                               var_idx:var_idx+compset.phase_record.phase_dof] = \
371	                mass_jac_tmp_view[:compset.phase_record.num_internal_cons, num_statevars:num_statevars+compset.phase_record.phase_dof]
372	            for iter_idx in range(num_statevars):
373	                for idx in range(compset.phase_record.num_internal_cons):
374	                    mass_jac[constraint_offset + idx, iter_idx] += \
375	                        mass_jac_tmp_view[idx, iter_idx]
376	            mass_jac_tmp[:,:] = 0
377	            var_idx += compset.phase_record.phase_dof
378	            constraint_offset += compset.phase_record.num_internal_cons
379	        # Second: Active inequality constraints
380	        for idx in range(num_active_ineq):
381	            mass_jac[constraint_offset, active_ineq[idx]] = 1
382	            constraint_offset += 1
383	        # Third: Mass constraints for pure elements
384	        mass_grad = self.mass_gradient(x_in).T
385	        var_idx = 0
386	        for grad_idx in range(constraint_offset, mass_jac.shape[0]):
387	            for var_idx in range(self.num_vars):
388	                mass_jac[grad_idx, var_idx] = mass_grad[grad_idx - constraint_offset, var_idx]
389	        return np.array(mass_jac)

391	    def chemical_potentials(self, x_in):
392	        "Assuming the input is a feasible solution."
393	        # mu = (A+) grad
394	        jac_pinv = np.linalg.pinv(self.mass_jacobian(x_in).T)
395	        mu = np.dot(jac_pinv, self.gradient(x_in))[-len(self.nonvacant_elements):]
396	        return mu

398	    def chemical_potential_gradient(self, x_in):
399	        "Assuming the input is a feasible solution."
400	        # mu' = (A+)' grad + (A+) hess
401	        jac = self.mass_jacobian(x_in).T
402	        jac_pinv = np.linalg.pinv(jac)
403	        # Axes swap needed for compatibility with _pinv_derivative
404	        mass_hess = np.swapaxes(self.mass_cons_hessian(x_in), 0, 1)
405	        hess = self.obj_hessian(x_in)
406	        grad = self.gradient(x_in)
407	        jac_pinv_prime = _pinv_derivative(jac, jac_pinv, mass_hess)
408	        mu_prime = np.dot(jac_pinv, hess) + np.einsum('ijk,j->ik', jac_pinv_prime, grad)
409	        return mu_prime[-len(self.nonvacant_elements):]

7	import numpy as np
8	
9	def cartesian(arrays, out=None):
10	    """
11	    Generate a cartesian product of input arrays.
12	    Source: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/1208118/using-numpy-to-build-an-array-of-all-combinations-of-two-arrays
13	
14	    Parameters
15	    ----------
16	    arrays : list of array-like
17	        1-D arrays to form the cartesian product of.
18	    out : ndarray
19	        Array to place the cartesian product in.
20	
21	    Returns
22	    -------
23	    out : ndarray
24	        2-D array of shape (M, len(arrays)) containing cartesian products
25	        formed of input arrays.
26	
27	    Examples
28	    --------
29	    >>> cartesian(([1, 2, 3], [4, 5], [6, 7]))
30	    array([[1, 4, 6],
31	           [1, 4, 7],
32	           [1, 5, 6],
33	           [1, 5, 7],
34	           [2, 4, 6],
35	           [2, 4, 7],
36	           [2, 5, 6],
37	           [2, 5, 7],
38	           [3, 4, 6],
39	           [3, 4, 7],
40	           [3, 5, 6],
41	           [3, 5, 7]])
42	
43	    """
44	
45	    arrays = [np.asarray(x) for x in arrays]
46	    dtype = arrays[0].dtype
47	
48	    n = np.prod([x.size for x in arrays])
49	    if out is None:
50	        out = np.zeros([n, len(arrays)], dtype=dtype)
51	
52	    m = int(n / arrays[0].size)
53	    out[:, 0] = np.repeat(arrays[0], m)
54	    if arrays[1:]:
55	        cartesian(arrays[1:], out=out[0:m, 1:])
56	        for j in np.arange(1, arrays[0].size):
57	            out[j*m:(j+1)*m, 1:] = out[0:m, 1:]
58	    return out

102	        extra_points = [first_em * lingrid[np.newaxis].T +
103	                        second_em * lingrid[::-1][np.newaxis].T
104	                        for first_em, second_em in em_pairs]
105	        points = np.concatenate(list(itertools.chain([points], extra_points)))

17	def point_sample(comp_count, pdof=10):
18	    """
19	    Sample 'pdof * (sum(comp_count) - len(comp_count))' points in
20	    composition space for the sublattice configuration specified
21	    by 'comp_count'. Points are sampled quasi-randomly from a Halton sequence.
22	    A Halton sequence is like a uniform random distribution, but the
23	    result will always be the same for a given 'comp_count' and 'pdof'.
24	    Note: For systems with only one component, only one point will be
25	    returned, regardless of 'pdof'. This is because the degrees of freedom
26	    are zero for that case.
27	
28	    Parameters
29	    ----------
30	    comp_count : list
31	        Number of components in each sublattice.
32	    pdof : int
33	        Number of points to sample per degree of freedom.
34	
35	    Returns
36	    -------
37	    ndarray of generated points satisfying the mass balance.
38	
39	    Examples
40	    --------
41	    >>> comps = [8,1] # 8 components in sublattice 1; only 1 in sublattice 2
42	    >>> pts = point_sample(comps, pdof=20) # 7 d.o.f, returns a 140x7 ndarray
43	    """
44	    # Generate Halton sequence with appropriate dimensions and size
45	    pts = halton(sum(comp_count),
46	                 pdof * (sum(comp_count) - len(comp_count)), scramble=True)
47	    # Convert low-discrepancy sequence to normalized exponential
48	    # This will be uniformly distributed over the simplices
49	    pts = -np.log(pts)
50	    cur_idx = 0
51	    for ctx in comp_count:
52	        end_idx = cur_idx + ctx
53	        pts[:, cur_idx:end_idx] /= pts[:, cur_idx:end_idx].sum(axis=1)[:, None]
54	        cur_idx = end_idx
55	
56	    if len(pts) == 0:
57	        pts = np.atleast_2d([1] * len(comp_count))
58	    return pts

96	        # Eventually, this code should be able to collapse Piecewise's

100	            unmatching = []

77	def _parse_action(func):
78	    """
79	    Decorator for pyparsing parse actions to ease debugging.
80	
81	    pyparsing uses trial & error to deduce the number of arguments a parse
82	    action accepts. Unfortunately any ``TypeError`` raised by a parse action
83	    confuses that mechanism.

85	    This decorator replaces the trial & error mechanism with one based on
86	    reflection. If the decorated function itself raises a ``TypeError`` then
87	    that exception is re-raised if the wrapper is called with less arguments
88	    than required. This makes sure that the actual ``TypeError`` bubbles up
89	    from the call to the parse action (instead of the one caused by pyparsing's
90	    trial & error).

92	    Modified slightly from the original for Py3 compatibility
93	    Source: Florian Brucker on StackOverflow
94	    http://stackoverflow.com/questions/10177276/pyparsing-setparseaction-function-is-getting-no-arguments
95	    """
96	    func_items = inspect.signature(func).parameters.items()
97	    func_args = [name for name, param in func_items
98	                 if param.kind == param.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD]
99	    num_args = len(func_args)
100	    if num_args > 3:
101	        raise ValueError('Input function must take at most 3 parameters.')
102	
103	    @functools.wraps(func)
104	    def action(*args):
105	        "Wrapped function."
106	        if len(args) < num_args:
107	            if action.exc_info:
108	                raise action.exc_info[0](action.exc_info[1], action.exc_info[2])
109	        action.exc_info = None
110	        try:
111	            return func(*args[:-(num_args + 1):-1])
112	        except TypeError as err:
113	            action.exc_info = sys.exc_info()
114	            raise err

116	    action.exc_info = None
117	    return action

1	""""Common pyparsing grammar patterns."""
2	
3	from pyparsing import alphas, nums
4	from pyparsing import Group, OneOrMore, Optional, Regex, Suppress, Word
5	import re
6	
7	pos_neg_int_number = Word('+-' + nums).setParseAction(lambda t: [int(t[0])])  # '+3' or '-2' are examples
8	# matching float w/ regex is ugly but is recommended by pyparsing
9	regex_after_decimal = r'([0-9]*\.?[0-9]+([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?)'
10	float_number = Regex(r'[-+]?([0-9]+\.(?!([0-9]|[eE])))|{0}'.format(regex_after_decimal)) \
11	    .setParseAction(lambda t: [float(t[0])])
12	
13	chemical_formula = Group(OneOrMore(Word(alphas, min=1, max=2) + Optional(float_number, default=1.0))) + \
14	                   Optional(Suppress('/') + pos_neg_int_number, default=0)
15	
16	reg_symbol = r'([A-z][A-z]?)'
17	reg_amount = r'([-+]?([0-9]+\.(?!([0-9]|[eE])))|([0-9]*\.?[0-9]+([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?))?'
18	reg_charge = r'/([+-]?[0-9]+)'
19	chem_regex = reg_symbol + reg_amount
20	
21	def parse_chemical_formula(formula):
22	    """"""
23	    matches = re.findall(chem_regex, formula)
24	    sym_amnts = [(m[0], float(m[1]) if m[1] != '' else 1.0) for m in matches]
25	    charge = re.search(reg_charge, formula)
26	    if charge is None:
27	        charge = 0
28	    else:

96	        root[:] = [root, root, None, None]      # initialize by pointing to self
97	        nonlocal_root = [root]                  # make updateable non-locally
98	        PREV, NEXT, KEY, RESULT = 0, 1, 2, 3    # names for the link fields
99	
100	        if maxsize == 0:
101	
102	            def wrapper(*args, **kwds):
103	                # no caching, just do a statistics update after a successful call
104	                result = user_function(*args, **kwds)
105	                stats[MISSES] += 1
106	                return result
107	
108	        elif maxsize is None:

110	            def wrapper(*args, **kwds):
111	                # simple caching without ordering or size limit
112	                key = make_key(args, kwds, typed)
113	                result = cache_get(key, root)   # root used here as a unique not-found sentinel
114	                if result is not root:
115	                    stats[HITS] += 1
116	                    return result
117	                result = user_function(*args, **kwds)
118	                cache[key] = result
119	                stats[MISSES] += 1
120	                return result

122	        else:

124	            def wrapper(*args, **kwds):

126	                key = make_key(args, kwds, typed)
127	                with lock:
128	                    link = cache_get(key)
129	                    if link is not None:
130	                        # record recent use of the key by moving it to the front of the list
131	                        root, = nonlocal_root
132	                        link_prev, link_next, key, result = link
133	                        link_prev[NEXT] = link_next
134	                        link_next[PREV] = link_prev
135	                        last = root[PREV]
136	                        last[NEXT] = root[PREV] = link
137	                        link[PREV] = last
138	                        link[NEXT] = root
139	                        stats[HITS] += 1
140	                        return result
141	                result = user_function(*args, **kwds)
142	                with lock:
143	                    root, = nonlocal_root
144	                    if key in cache:

146	                        # cache while the lock was released.  since the link
147	                        # update is already done, we need only return the
148	                        # computed result and update the count of misses.
149	                        pass
150	                    elif _len(cache) >= maxsize:
151	                        # use the old root to store the new key and result
152	                        oldroot = root
153	                        oldroot[KEY] = key
154	                        oldroot[RESULT] = result
155	                        # empty the oldest link and make it the new root
156	                        root = nonlocal_root[0] = oldroot[NEXT]
157	                        oldkey = root[KEY]
158	                        oldvalue = root[RESULT]
159	                        root[KEY] = root[RESULT] = None
160	                        # now update the cache dictionary for the new links
161	                        del cache[oldkey]
162	                        cache[key] = oldroot
163	                    else:

165	                        last = root[PREV]

167	                        last[NEXT] = root[PREV] = cache[key] = link

    def atomic_ordering_energy(self, dbe):
        """
        Return the atomic ordering contribution in symbolic form.
        Description follows Servant and Ansara, Calphad, 2001.
        """
        phase = dbe.phases[self.phase_name]
        ordered_phase_name = phase.model_hints.get('ordered_phase', None)
        disordered_phase_name = phase.model_hints.get('disordered_phase', None)
        if phase.name != ordered_phase_name:
            return S.Zero
        disordered_model = self.__class__(dbe, sorted(self.components),
                                          disordered_phase_name)
        constituents = [sorted(set(c).intersection(self.components)) \
                for c in dbe.phases[ordered_phase_name].constituents]

        # Fix variable names
        variable_rename_dict = {}
        disordered_sitefracs = [x for x in disordered_model.energy.free_symbols if isinstance(x, v.SiteFraction)]
        for atom in disordered_sitefracs:
            # Replace disordered phase site fractions with mole fractions of
            # ordered phase site fractions.
            # Special case: Pure vacancy sublattices
            all_species_in_sublattice = \
                dbe.phases[disordered_phase_name].constituents[
                    atom.sublattice_index]
            if atom.species.name == 'VA' and len(all_species_in_sublattice) == 1:
                # Assume: Pure vacancy sublattices are always last
                vacancy_subl_index = \
                    len(dbe.phases[ordered_phase_name].constituents)-1
                variable_rename_dict[atom] = \
                    v.SiteFraction(
                        ordered_phase_name, vacancy_subl_index, atom.species)
            else:
                # All other cases: replace site fraction with mole fraction
                variable_rename_dict[atom] = \
                    self.mole_fraction(
                        atom.species,
                        ordered_phase_name,
                        constituents,
                        dbe.phases[ordered_phase_name].sublattices
                        )
        # Save all of the ordered energy contributions
        # This step is why this routine must be called _last_ in build_phase
        ordered_energy = Add(*list(self.models.values()))
        self.models.clear()
        # Copy the disordered energy contributions into the correct bins
        for name, value in disordered_model.models.items():
            self.models[name] = value.xreplace(variable_rename_dict)
        # All magnetic parameters will be defined in the disordered model
        self.TC = self.curie_temperature = disordered_model.TC
        self.TC = self.curie_temperature = self.TC.xreplace(variable_rename_dict)

        molefraction_dict = {}

        # Construct a dictionary that replaces every site fraction with its
        # corresponding mole fraction in the disordered state
        ordered_sitefracs = [x for x in ordered_energy.free_symbols if isinstance(x, v.SiteFraction)]
        for sitefrac in ordered_sitefracs:
            all_species_in_sublattice = \
                dbe.phases[ordered_phase_name].constituents[
                    sitefrac.sublattice_index]
            if sitefrac.species.name == 'VA' and len(all_species_in_sublattice) == 1:
                # pure-vacancy sublattices should not be replaced
                # this handles cases like AL,NI,VA:AL,NI,VA:VA and
                # ensures the VA's don't get mixed up
                continue
            molefraction_dict[sitefrac] = \
                self.mole_fraction(sitefrac.species,
                                   ordered_phase_name, constituents,
                                   dbe.phases[ordered_phase_name].sublattices)

        return ordered_energy - ordered_energy.xreplace(molefraction_dict)

def true_equilibrium(dbf_path, comps, phases, T, x_al, pdens=3000):
    dbf = Database(dbf_path)

    # gather (GM, x) per point across all phases
    xs = res.X.values.reshape(-1, len(comps)-1) if len(comps) == 3 else None
    gms = res.GM.values.reshape(-1)
    phs = res.Phase.values.reshape(-1)
    m = np.isfinite(gms)
    xs, gms, phs = xs[m], gms[m], phs[m]
    # single-phase best
    d = np.abs(xs[:, 0] - x_al)
    i1 = np.argmin(d - (gms - gms.min()) * 0)
    best = (gms[np.abs(xs[:, 0] - x_al) < 1e-6].min(initial=np.inf), 'single')
    # two-phase search
    best_g = np.inf
    best_desc = None
    for i, j in combinations(range(len(gms)), 2):
        xa, xb = xs[i, 0], xs[j, 0]
        if abs(xa - xb) < 1e-9:

        f = (x_al - xb) / (xa - xb)

def filter_phases(dbf, comps, candidate_phases=None):
    """Return phases that are valid for equilibrium calculations for the given database and components

    def all_sublattices_active(comps, phase):

                              subl in phase.constituents]

    if candidate_phases == None:

    else:
        candidate_phases = set(candidate_phases).intersection(dbf.phases.keys())
    disordered_phases = [dbf.phases[phase].model_hints.get('disordered_phase') for phase in candidate_phases]
    phases = [phase for phase in candidate_phases if
                all_sublattices_active(comps, dbf.phases[phase]) and
                (phase not in disordered_phases or (phase in disordered_phases and
                dbf.phases[phase].model_hints.get('ordered_phase') not in candidate_phases))]
